public_rationale: Microsoft's Q1 FY2026 ended September 30, 2025; its release gives total revenue but no OpenAI revenue share [e1]. The located 11% report concerns July–September 2026, so it neither establishes nor disproves the share in the named quarter [e2]. Reuters, citing Wall Street Journal reporting, gives OpenAI's July–September 2026 operating loss as $10.9 billion; this supports the amount on an operating-loss basis [e3]. Bloomberg reported roughly $11 billion wired by November 6, 2026, at a $1.25 trillion valuation, against initial targets of at least $30 billion and $1.4 trillion [e5]. The financing figures therefore have support as of November 6, but the round remained open and these reports do not establish the total through November 17 [e4] [e5]. The missing matched-quarter revenue share and unspecified loss basis leave the compound claim unresolved [e1] [e2] [e3].
limitations: The September 2026 revenue-share report cannot substitute for evidence covering July–September 2025 [e1] [e2].
The loss report identifies operating loss, not net loss, and relies on attributed reporting rather than public OpenAI financial statements [e3].
The funding reports establish an initial close, not the November 17 total or final round size [e4] [e5].
Microsoft's total revenue does not establish AI revenue outside OpenAI [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI made up 11% of Microsoft's total revenues in Q1 FY2026, which the author says suggests Microsoft's overall revenues are in decline and its AI revenues aren't filling the gap outside OpenAI, which lost $10.9 billion in Q3 2026 and raised only $11 billion of the $30 billion it wanted at a $1.25 trillion valuation, lower than expected.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI made up 11% of Microsoft’s total revenues in Q1 Fiscal Year 2026, which suggests that Microsoft’s overall revenues are in decline and that its AI revenues aren’t filling the gap

from_speaker: raised only $11 billion of the $30 billion it wanted
our_interpretation: The firm assertions concern the revenue share, loss, funding amount, funding target and valuation.

The words 'which suggests' make the Microsoft revenue-decline and AI-shortfall statements tentative inferences. They are discussed but are not converted into firm assertions or required to be proved for support.
Q1 FY2026 is retained as written. It is not silently changed to Q1 FY2027.
Q3 2026 for OpenAI is read as July–September 2026 because no fiscal calendar is supplied.
The funding statement concerns the amount raised by publication, not a claim that the round had permanently closed at $11 billion.

The target-period envelope contains separate subperiods: Microsoft's named fiscal quarter, OpenAI's third calendar quarter of 2026, and its latest financing through November 17. Evidence must match the relevant subperiod.

The structured metric_scope records the leading Microsoft revenue-share assertion. OpenAI loss, financing and valuation are separate metrics, recorded on their evidence items rather than treated as interchangeable.
The supplied sentence does not identify the accounting basis or source of the financial figures. An operating-loss report cannot automatically establish an unspecified net loss.
criteria.support_condition: Matched-period evidence establishes the approximately 11% Microsoft revenue share in Q1 FY2026, the specified OpenAI quarterly loss on a matching basis, and approximately $11 billion raised toward an original $30 billion goal at a $1.25 trillion valuation below the earlier target. The tentative Microsoft inference is not scored as a firm assertion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched-company, matched-period and matched-basis evidence materially disproves one or more firm numerical assertions. Evidence from Q1 FY2027 alone cannot disprove a Q1 FY2026 revenue share.

evidence.locator: FY26 Q1 earnings release, closing information-date statement
evidence.explanation: The release identifies Q1 FY2026 as the September 2025 quarter and reports total revenue of $77.7 billion, up 18% year over year. It establishes the period and denominator, but supplies no matching OpenAI revenue numerator.

evidence.locator: Earnings-call discussion, paragraph beginning 'Later in the call'
evidence.explanation: The article reports approximately $10 billion from OpenAI, about 11% of Microsoft's revenue, for the September 2026 quarter. This is evidence of a likely fiscal-year error, but it cannot establish or disprove the share in September 2025.

Reuters attributes the $10.9 billion quarterly figure to Wall Street Journal reporting and identifies it as an operating loss. It corroborates the amount under that reading, but does not establish an unspecified net-loss figure.
The report corroborates the financing amount and valuation and says the round had not yet closed. It supports a raised-so-far reading, not a permanent final shortfall.

evidence.locator: Paragraph discussing the reduced fundraising goals
evidence.explanation: Bloomberg reports that the initial funds had been wired and contrasts the $1.25 trillion valuation with an earlier $1.4 trillion target. It also identifies the original fundraising goal as $30 billion or more, corroborating the historical targets without establishing the final round size.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Matched-period disclosure of Microsoft's revenue attributable to OpenAI for July–September 2025; clarification and records of OpenAI's intended loss measure for July–September 2026; and a financing update establishing funds received through November 17, 2026.
